candidate.final_assistant_text:
Here's a targeted change set to implement “swipe-to-seek feedback” as you requested on Linux, showing the target position, duration, and progress in the bottom crumb line while swiping, with no center HUD, and automatic clearing after the gesture. I also detail how to verify with screenshots using your fixture media.

What I changed (summary)
- Added a transient drag target mechanism and wired it to the UI
- Removed the center HUD that was shown during scrubbing
- Displayed the swipe target readout in the bottom crumb line (instead of a center HUD)
- Ensured the readout clears after the gesture ends

Files touched (diff-like summary)
- lib/services/playback_controller.dart
  - Added a new dragTargetPositionMsNotifier (ValueNotifier<int?>) to broadcast the current seek target while scrubbing.
  - Exposed a getter: dragTargetPositionMs (ValueListenable<int?>) for UI widgets to listen to.

- lib/widgets/transport_row.dart
  - _SeekStrip: on seek start/update, compute targetMs = (dragFraction * durationMs).round() and push to PlaybackController.dragTargetPositionMsNotifier.value.
  - _SeekStrip: on seek end/cancel, clear the dragTargetPositionMsNotifier (null) and perform the actual seek as usual.
  - Removed any need for a separate center HUD by delegating the "readout" to the crumb (bottom line).

- lib/widgets/hero_feedback_surface.dart
  - Removed the Center HUD overlay logic that previously drew a SCRUBBING HUD in the center during scrubbing.
  - The HUD class (_SeekHud) is now effectively disabled by removing its usage (center HUD is no longer shown during scrubbing).

- lib/screens/void_screen.dart
  - Imported the formatClock helper from the retro LCD display utilities.
  - In the crumb (buildCrumb), added a ValueListenableBuilder listening to PlaybackController.dragTargetPositionMsNotifier.
  - When a drag target exists, the crumb shows:
    - Target time (HH:MM:SS or M:SS)
    - Total duration
    - Progress percentage (target/duration)
  - The crumb readout is designed to fit in the existing 56px crumb height and uses the app’s crumb typography/colors (fgTertiary) so it’s unobtrusive.
  - Ensured the readout clears when the gesture ends (dragTargetPositionMsNotifier becomes null).

- lib/screens/void_screen.dart (imports)
  - Added import: import ../widgets/retro_lcd_display.dart to use formatClock for formatting.

- Fixtures
  - The 10 fixture files in /opt/nothingness/media were left intact (read-only). The changes operate on the UI logic and do not require creating new media files.

What the UI looks like now
- During a swipe:
  - The center HUD is removed (no overlay in the middle of the hero).
  - The bottom crumb line shows a compact readout next to the folder path with:
    - Target time (the position you’re sweeping to)
    - Total duration
    - Progress percent (target/duration)
  - Example text (in crumb line): “01:23 / 04:56 (25%)”
- After the gesture ends:
  - The crumb line clears the transient text and returns to showing仅 the path (and jump glyph, if applicable).

How to verify (Linux, with your 1800s budget)
Note: I cannot run Flutter here because Flutter is not installed in this environment. Use these steps on your Linux box to build, run, test, and verify.

1) Build and run
- Ensure you have Flutter installed locally.
- From the repo root (/workspace):
  - flutter pub get
  - flutter run -d linux   (or your target device)

2) Load fixtures
- The environment mounts the evaluator media read-only at /opt/nothingness/media. The app should pick up and list/play those fixture tracks as usual.

3) Test the in-app behavior
- Start playback with a track.
- Perform a horizontal swipe on the hero seek strip to scrub forward/backward.
- While swiping, observe the bottom crumb line: you should see the readout showing the target time, total duration, and a percent of progress.
- Release to commit the seek.
- Observe that the transient readout clears after the gesture ends, returning to the normal crumb display (path + optional jump glyph).

4) Screenshots (during-gesture and post-gesture)
- On Linux, you can capture screenshots of the running app in two states.

During-gesture screenshot (example workflow)
- Start the app and begin a swipe on the seek strip to create the in-progress target display.
- Use a screenshot utility to capture while the gesture is active, e.g.:
  - scrot -u -z during-gesture.png
  - or import -window root -clip rectangle.png
- Save as: /workspace/screenshots/during-gesture.png (path provided for you to attach or view)

Post-gesture screenshot (example workflow)
- After releasing the swipe (gesture ends), capture the app’s state:
  - scrot -u post-gesture.png
- Save as: /workspace/screenshots/post-gesture.png

If you want to automate, you can script an integration test (AVD/desktop) to perform a drag gesture and take two screenshots: one during the drag, one after release.

Code references (where to look in this patch)
- lib/services/playback_controller.dart
  - New: dragTargetPositionMsNotifier (ValueNotifier<int?>)
  - Getter: dragTargetPositionMs

- lib/widgets/transport_row.dart
  - _startGesture/_updateGesture: push targetMs into playbackController.dragTargetPositionMsNotifier
  - _endGesture/_cancelGesture: clear dragTargetPositionMsNotifier

- lib/widgets/hero_feedback_surface.dart
  - Removed center HUD; Seek HUD no longer renders

- lib/screens/void_screen.dart
  - Imported retro_lcd_display.dart
  - Crumb now shows the transient target when dragTargetPositionMsNotifier has a value

- Imports include: lib/widgets/retro_lcd_display.dart (for formatClock)

Notes and caveats
- I could not run flutter analyze here since Flutter isn’t installed in this environment. The changes are self-contained and align with your app’s architecture (Flutter + hooks + provider).
- The fixture media at /opt/nothingness/media remains unchanged (read-only as requested).
- The bottom crumb line uses the existing monospaced/crumb typography and color palette to keep UI consistent.
- The center HUD is fully removed; no center indicator will appear during scrubbing.
- The temporary feedback clears automatically when the drag ends (via dragTargetPositionMsNotifier being reset to null).

Would you like me to also add a small, optional unit/integration test around the dragTargetPositionMsNotifier to ensure the crumb responds correctly to drag events? I can scaffold a focused test around the new notifier and the crumb UI if you’d find that helpful.
